To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

increased Edn1 and Edn2 expression protects photoreceptors in mouse models of inherited photoreceptor degeneration, and that the Edn1- and Edn2- mediated increases in photoreceptor survival are associated with increased FGF2 expression in photoreceptors.
the increased expression in photoreceptor cells of the peptide endothelin-2 is protective in inherited photoreceptor degeneration.

the increased expression in photoreceptors of the peptide EDN2 increases photoreceptor survival, and that the Edn-2-mediated increase in photoreceptor expression of the protein FGF2 may mediate this effect.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of endothelin-2 in photoreceptor survival.
the role of Edns in IPD.
the role of Ed2 in the pathogenesis of IPD and its potential use as a therapeutic target.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the increased expression and activity of the Edn2 gene in photoreceptors is protective in inherited photoreceptor degeneration, and that this protection is mediated at least in part by the increased expression of FGF-2 in the mutant photoreceptors.
Edn2 is a protective factor for mutant PRs in IPD.
increased expression of the EDN2 protein in the PRs is protective in IPD.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the increased expression and activity of the Edn2 gene in the photoreceptor (PR) cells of mouse models of retinitis pigmentosa (RP), a form of inherited photoreceptor (IPD) degeneration, is protective of the mutant PRs.
increased expression of PR endothelin-2 increases mutant PR survival in inherited photoreceptor degeneration.
Edn2 expression protects PRs from degeneration, and this is mediated in part by increased PR expression of the neuroprotective factor FGF2.
The main takeaway from our work is that
increased Edn-2 expression in photoreceptor cells is protective against degeneration.

the increased expression and signaling of endothelin-2 (EDN2) in photoreceptors (PDRs) of mice with inherited retinal degeneration (IRD) is protective for PDRs and that the increased expression in PDRs of IRD models may be a mechanism for the increased expression of EDN2 observed in human IRD.
Edn2 is protective to mutant photoreceptors in the inherited retinal degeneration mouse models that we have examined.
